note.explanation: A body is in equilibrium when it has no acceleration. It may be at rest (static equilibrium) or move with uniform velocity (dynamic equilibrium). Forces balance when their resultant is zero.
examples: A book resting on a table is in static equilibrium: the table’s upward normal force balances the book’s downward weight.
A paratrooper descending with uniform velocity is in dynamic equilibrium: air resistance balances gravity.
note.checkAnswer: A body moving with uniform velocity is in dynamic equilibrium.
note.simple: Equilibrium means there is no change in the body's motion: it stays at rest or keeps moving at the same velocity.
note.checkQuestion: What type of equilibrium describes a body moving with uniform velocity?
note.title: Equilibrium: balanced forces, no acceleration
steps: Check whether the body has acceleration.
If it has no acceleration, it is in equilibrium.
If it is at rest, it is in static equilibrium.
If it moves with uniform velocity, it is in dynamic equilibrium.
Forces acting on it balance when their resultant is zero.

options: It must have zero forces acting on it.
It must be moving with uniform velocity.
mcqs.stem: Which statement describes a body in equilibrium?
rationales: This is correct because the textbook defines equilibrium as having no acceleration.
This is wrong because a body moving with uniform velocity can also be in equilibrium.
This is wrong because forces may act but balance each other.
This is wrong because a body at rest can also be in equilibrium.

mcqs.stem: A book lies motionless on a table. What is its state of equilibrium?
rationales: This is wrong because dynamic equilibrium describes motion with uniform velocity.
This is correct because a body at rest is in static equilibrium.
This is wrong because the book has no acceleration and its forces balance.
This is wrong because the book is supported by the table rather than falling freely.

mcqs.stem: A body moves in a straight line with uniform velocity and has no acceleration. What kind of equilibrium is this?
rationales: This is wrong because static equilibrium describes a body at rest.
This is correct because a body moving with uniform velocity is in dynamic equilibrium.
This is wrong because no acceleration means the body is in equilibrium.
This is wrong because equilibrium requires no acceleration.

options: The body remains at rest or continues with uniform velocity.
mcqs.stem: When the resultant force on a body is zero, what can happen to it?
rationales: This is correct: it can remain at rest or continue moving with uniform velocity.
This is wrong because a zero resultant force does not cause the body to speed up.
This is wrong because a zero resultant force does not cause a change in velocity.
This is wrong because a zero resultant force does not make a moving body stop.

options: The book’s weight is greater than the normal force.
The normal force balances the book’s weight.
The book has no forces acting on it.
The table pulls the book downward.
mcqs.stem: A book rests on a table. Which statement explains why it remains in equilibrium?
rationales: This is wrong because unequal forces would give the book a resultant force.
This is correct because the upward normal force equals the downward weight.
This is wrong because both the weight and normal force act on the book.
This is wrong because the normal force from the table acts upward.

options: The paratrooper has no forces acting on them.
Air resistance acts downward and is greater than gravity.
mcqs.stem: A paratrooper descends with uniform velocity. Which forces are balanced?
rationales: This is correct because upward air resistance balances downward gravity.
This is wrong because gravity acts downward on the paratrooper.
This is wrong because gravity and air resistance both act on the paratrooper.
This is wrong because air resistance acts upward and balances gravity.

options: Forces can act on a body without accelerating it if they balance.
Any force makes a body accelerate.
Only bodies at rest can have forces acting on them.
A body in equilibrium has no weight.
mcqs.stem: Which statement about forces on a body in equilibrium is correct?
rationales: This is correct because balanced forces can act without accelerating the body.
This is wrong because a body's acceleration depends on the resultant force, not merely the presence of a force.
This is wrong because forces can act on moving bodies too.
This is wrong because a body can have weight while in equilibrium.

example.question: A book lies on a table. Explain why it is in static equilibrium.
example.answer: The book is in static equilibrium because it is at rest and the upward normal force balances its downward weight: F_n = w.

explain.title: Equilibrium means no acceleration
explain.body: Your textbook defines it this way: “A body is said to be in equilibrium if it has no acceleration.” Forces may act on the body, but they must balance so their resultant is zero.

explain.title: Static equilibrium
explain.body: “A body at rest is in static equilibrium whereas a body moving with uniform velocity is in dynamic equilibrium.” A book lying on a table is a static example: its upward normal force balances its downward weight.

explain.title: Dynamic equilibrium
explain.body: A body can move and still be in equilibrium if its velocity is uniform. A paratrooper descending with uniform velocity is in dynamic equilibrium because air resistance balances gravity.

explain.title: Balanced forces can act
explain.body: Equilibrium does not mean that no forces act. It means the forces balance, so the body has no acceleration.

mistakes: Do not say a body in equilibrium must be at rest; uniform-velocity motion is dynamic equilibrium.
Do not say that no forces act on an object in equilibrium. Forces can act and balance each other.
Do not confuse uniform velocity with changing speed or direction; changing velocity means acceleration.
